libpcap is a system-level library (packet capture, sockets, netlink). The pcap-linux.c patch addresses a real sockaddr_storage header conflict on HarmonyOS. test_package tests pcap_lib_version() and pcap_findalldevs() which exercise system interface integration. However, actual packet capture (pcap_open_live/pcap_loop) is not tested. Flagged for manual verification of adaptation completeness — see P3-006.

findings.rule: review_memory §1.7 — R40 深度适配验证
findings.description: libpcap is a system-level packet capture library interfacing with raw sockets, netlink, and procfs. The test_package only tests pcap_lib_version() (metadata) and pcap_findalldevs() (device enumeration). It does not test actual packet capture (pcap_open_live, pcap_next, pcap_loop). While the sockaddr_storage fix is a real adaptation, the capture path is untested.
findings.recommendation: Flag for manual verification: confirm that pcap_open_live/pcap_compile/pcap_setfilter work on HarmonyOS. Consider adding a test that opens a pcap handle on 'any' interface (may require root/cap_net_raw).

findings.rule: review_memory §1.7 — R40 深度适配验证
findings.description: The pcap-linux.c patch resolves a sockaddr_storage redefinition by #define-redirecting before including linux/if.h. This is a valid workaround, but it relies on the assumption that linux/if.h is the only source of the conflicting definition. If other headers also define sockaddr_storage, additional guards may be needed.
findings.recommendation: Verify that the #define/#undef approach fully resolves the conflict across all compilation units, not just pcap-linux.c.

findings.description: The docstring says 'Build system: cmake.' which is correct, but the config.guess/config.sub patches suggest autotools was initially attempted. The docstring could mention that autotools was abandoned in favor of cmake for clarity.
findings.recommendation: Optional: add a note in the docstring about the build system choice rationale.
